podcast.body: This song was Simon & Garfunkel's biggest hit before they broke up, bidding farewell to the 1960s. It is essentially a gospel song and was replaced at number one in 1970 by The Beatles' "Let It Be." Aretha Franklin covered it, and it defeated The Carpenters' "Close to You" and The Guess Who's "American Woman" for the year-end title. "Bridge over troubled water is essentially a gospel song."

podcast.body: This song was the longest-reigning number one hit of 1970, staying at the top of the charts for six weeks. It is considered "as gospel influenced as any song of the early 1970s." "Bridge Over Troubled Water by Simon and Garfunkel. It was number one for six weeks and it is as gospel influenced as any song of the early 1970s."

podcast.body: This song, composed by Paul Simon, reached number one a year before Aretha Franklin released her cover. Franklin's version, a full-on gospel hymn, reached number 6 on the Hot 100 and number 1 on the R&B chart. "A year after Simon and Garfunkel took bridge over troubled water to number 1."

podcast.body: This title track was Billboard's top single of 1970. It swept Record and Song of the Year prizes at the 1971 Grammy Awards, alongside its album counterpart. "The LP and its title track were billboards top album and single of 1970. And accordingly, they swept the album, record and song of the year prizes at the 1971 Grammys."
